title: Even if you couldn’t make it to Fringe this year, you can still check...
transcript: Edinburgh Fringe is the world's largest theatre festival. But if you weren't able to make it, here's four cast recordings from shows that I loved that you can listen to right now and stick around, because I guarantee you there are shows on this list that you've never heard of that could be your next musical theatre obsession. First up is Penelope. It is a retelling of the odyssey from Penelope's perspective as she waits for her husband to come home from war. When I first saw the show, I immediately booked tickets to come back and see it again. That's how good it is. And Grace McLean is truly giving an all time performance in the show. Next up is Hole!, which I've talked about a lot on this channel. It was a big hit at last year's fringe. It's now back at this year's fringe and about to do an off Broadway run in New York later this year. It is, I think, the funniest new musical I've listened to in a while. It is completely absurd, definitely a little not safe for work, but at its core, it's actually a really sweet, queer love story that is genuinely moving despite its absurd premise. Next is a show called The Real Kyle Mccaren, which was not on my radar at all, but it's being produced by the same people who did Operation Mincemeat and released a Studio E P. With some of the music featuring people like Jordan Fisher and Norbert Leo Butz. It is an incredibly moving meditation on grief and how we remember people who have passed, with a score that feels a bit like a throwback to, like, early 2000s indie musical theatre. Very Kerrigan and Lowdermilk. Finally, the newest release on this list, legendary, which just came out today. It is written and performed by Cheeyang Ng. And of all of the scores that I listened to at fringe, this is the one that got stuck in my head the most. The show beautifully weaves together their life story and Chinese mythology, and explores how we can chart our own paths while still honoring the legends and history that came before us.
